correctness.rationale: In the closed nonnegative SEIR system, \(\dot C=\beta SI=-\dot S\), so \(C(t)=C(0)+S(0)-S(t)\) and \(C\) converges because \(S\) is nonincreasing and bounded below. If two perfect sliding-window outputs agree, \(D(t)=C_1(t)-C_2(t)\) satisfies \(D(t+h)=D(t)\). Because \(D\) also converges, every periodic value equals the same limit, so \(D\) is constant. A constant shift of the auxiliary \(C\) state has no effect on \(S,E,I,R\) or the parameters, hence perfect window-incidence observation has exactly the same parameter equivalence relation as perfect cumulative-incidence observation. Equality of instantaneous incidences gives the same conclusion by integration. The parameter involution transcribed from the source preserves the three source input-output combinations and is checked exactly by the assigned verifier.
residual_risks: The result is for perfect continuous sliding-window data, not a finite list of nonoverlapping reported counts.
The convergence argument uses the closed no-demography SEIR model; it need not extend to forced or demographic models with unbounded cumulative incidence.

originality.rationale: Saucedo et al. analyze cumulative-incidence structural identifiability and report markedly better practical identifiability from incidence, but their incidence observable is a time difference of cumulative incidence and their structural tools did not resolve that difference output. The audited periodic-plus-convergent argument closes exactly that gap and proves that the practical improvement cannot come from a different perfect-data ambiguity class.
